edges.description: Failure of inhibitory GABA/glycine transmission leaves motor neuron activity unopposed, producing rigidity.
Unopposed activity within reflex arcs makes minor stimuli trigger spasms.
Disinhibition of autonomic neurons causes dysregulated catecholamine release.
Pharyngeal spasm from toxin-driven disinhibition impairs swallowing.
Laryngeal spasm from toxin-driven disinhibition causes airway obstruction and respiratory arrest.
Local toxin production by germinated C. tetani is the source of the toxin that reaches the nervous system.

nodes.description: Tetanus toxoid vaccine should be administered during recovery as natural infection does not confer immunity.

evidence.reference_title: Tetanus Toxoid Vaccination Coverage and Associated Factors among Childbearing Women in Ethiopia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.snippet: The pooled estimate of receiving at least two doses of tetanus toxoid immunization coverage in Ethiopia was 52.2% (95% CI: 42.47-61.93, I 2 = 98.4%).

nodes.description: Tetanus toxin affects the autonomic nervous system, causing sympathetic overactivity that manifests as tachycardia, hypertension, arrhythmias, and hyperthermia. This autonomic instability is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in severe tetanus.

evidence.snippet: C tetani releases a potent neurotoxin, causing muscle spasms, rigidity, and dysautonomia.

nodes.description: Difficulty swallowing due to pharyngeal muscle spasm, which increases risk of aspiration pneumonia.

evidence.snippet: Severe dysphagia resulting from pharyngeal spasm confers a high risk of aspiration.

nodes.description: Sustained muscle contraction affecting the entire body, including the characteristic "risus sardonicus" (sardonic smile) from facial muscle involvement.

evidence.snippet: C tetani releases a potent neurotoxin, causing muscle spasms, rigidity, and dysautonomia.

nodes.description: Painful, generalized muscle spasms triggered by minor stimuli such as noise, light, or touch. These spasms can be severe enough to cause fractures.

evidence.snippet: C tetani releases a potent neurotoxin, causing muscle spasms, rigidity, and dysautonomia.

nodes.description: Spasm of respiratory muscles and laryngospasm can cause life-threatening respiratory compromise, the leading cause of death in tetanus.

evidence.snippet: Important complications include laryngeal spasm and resultant airway obstruction and respiratory arrest.

nodes.description: Clostridium tetani produces tetanospasmin, a potent neurotoxin that is transported retrogradely along motor neurons to the spinal cord. The toxin blocks the release of inhibitory neurotransmitters (GABA and glycine) from presynaptic terminals in the spinal cord, leading to unopposed muscle contraction and characteristic spasms.

evidence.reference_title: Toxicology and pharmacology of botulinum and tetanus neurotoxins: an update.
evidence.snippet: Tetanus and botulinum neurotoxins cause the neuroparalytic syndromes of tetanus and botulism, respectively, by delivering inside different types of neurons, metalloproteases specifically cleaving the SNARE proteins that are essential for the release of neurotransmitters.

nodes.description: Clostridium tetani spores are ubiquitous in soil and enter the body through wounds. In anaerobic conditions (deep puncture wounds, necrotic tissue), spores germinate and the vegetative bacteria produce toxin locally before it spreads systemically.

evidence.snippet: Tetanus results from infections with spore-forming Clostridium tetani bacteria, usually acquired via contaminated wounds and burns.
